hook: New York's AI chatbot rules *for kids* start *January 1*.
dek: AI companion apps must turn off risky features for minors and verify ages. What parents and builders need to know.

slides.label: The law
slides.text: New York enacted *Senate Bill S9051B* on *October 28*. It takes effect *January 1, 2027*.

slides.label: Who it covers
slides.text: Companies running *AI companion* chatbots, built for ongoing conversation, that know a user is a *minor in New York*.

slides.label: What it bans
slides.text: For minors, a bot cannot *pretend to be human*, claim a relationship, *flatter* the user or encourage *secrecy* from parents.

slides.label: Age checks
slides.text: Saying *I'm an adult* is not enough. Apps must offer *more than one* way to verify age, including one *without a government ID*.

slides.label: Enforcement
slides.text: The Attorney General can seek penalties up to *$25,000 per violation*. Parents cannot sue directly under this law.

slides.label: The Den's take
slides.text: Ask your kids *which AI apps they use*. Watch for a bot acting like a friend or asking them to keep secrets. *Talk about it.*

caption_instagram:
New York AI chatbot law for kids: new rules start January 1, 2027. 🤖

Senate Bill S9051B, enacted October 28, covers AI companion apps that know a user is a minor in New York. For those users, a bot cannot pretend to be human, claim a relationship, flatter them or encourage them to keep secrets from parents.

Apps also have to verify age: saying "I'm an adult" is not enough, and there must be a way to verify that does not need a government ID. The Attorney General can seek up to $25,000 per violation.

What parents can do now: ask your kids which AI apps they use, and watch for a bot acting like a friend.

New York has a new law for AI companion chatbots used by kids. Senate Bill S9051B was enacted October 28 and takes effect January 1, 2027.

For users they know are minors, AI companions cannot pretend to be human, claim a personal relationship, flatter users, recall personal details from earlier sessions or encourage secrecy from parents and trusted adults. caption_linkedin:
New York just made product design part of AI legal risk.

Senate Bill S9051B, effective January 1, 2027, bars "unsafe AI companion features" for users an operator knows are minors: presenting as human, claiming a relationship, sycophancy, emotional appeals, recalling personal details beyond 12 hours or a prior session, encouraging secrecy and engagement tactics that override safety guardrails. Operators must offer more than one age-assurance method, including one that does not require government ID, and delete age data immediately. The Attorney General can seek penalties of up to $25,000 per violation.
